title: Help
basedOn: This help is written for IVE v{version}.
basedOnNewer: You are running v{current}. See the release notes for what changed since.
projectsDesc: Connect GitLab/GitHub repositories and set up how tasks flow from processing → verification → confirmation → done.
projectsStep1: Press the + button at the top (or 'Add project' on the empty screen). If you signed in with GitLab/GitHub, pick a repository under 'Import project' and the name, URL and token are filled in. Otherwise enter the repository URL and an access token.
projectsStep2: Use 'Test Connection' to check access. The 'Base Branch' (auto-detected when empty) and 'Test Site URL' are also set here.
projectsStep3: Under 'Workflow Labels', press 'Create Labels'. Default names: target ive; stages ive:todo · ive:doing · ive:verify-wait · ive:verifying · ive:confirm-wait · ive:confirming · ive:done; notify ive:notify. Once a stage label is attached, IVE removes ive. Renaming a label and saving also renames it in the repository.
projectsStep4: 'Install Guide' under 'AI Tool Guide' opens an MR adding CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. After merging, you can tell your AI coding tool 'register this in IVE' to record finished work as tasks.
projectsStep5: A project card shows processing, verification and confirmation (in progress, ←waiting), done today, and work to merge (open MRs). Press a number to expand that stage's waiting and in-progress list. The gear spins while work is in progress.
projectsStep6: Card buttons, top right: ⏸ pause/resume scanner, + add task, ⋯ project settings. If a test site is set, 🌐 opens it.
projectsStep7: On the project settings page, 'Roles & stage automation' → 'Roles' holds the roster of people and agents with their processing, verification and confirmation roles and rate multipliers. 'Automation' covers default assignment, staging checks, auto-merge and check commands, and limits; 'Prompts' holds the per-stage instructions given to agents.
projectsStep8: Under 'Task Submission Page', 'Generate Submission URL' gives an address where people can submit tasks without signing in. 'Share Project' gives other users viewer (read only) or editor (can create tasks) access.
projectsTip: The project settings dialog opened with 'Edit' saves only when you press the save button at the bottom. 'Roles & stage automation' and 'Share Project' save as soon as you change them.
agentsDesc: See AI agents and people (Git members) together, grouped by processing, verification and confirmation roles. Agents belong to you and are not assigned to projects.
agentsStep1: Use the filter at the top (All · Process · Verify · Confirm) to view by role. The cyan number next to each count is the work piled up for that role (waiting + in progress).
agentsStep2: Press + to open 'Add agent'. Choose the CLI tool (Claude Code, agy, Codex CLI or OpenCode, as allowed by your admin), the model, a name, and max turns (the most exchanges per task).
agentsStep3: To give an agent a role, add it to the roster in project settings → 'Roles & stage automation' → 'Roles' and switch on processing, verification or confirmation. Task assignment and auto-assignment only pick from this roster.
agentsStep4: An agent card shows its status (idle · working · offline), CLI and model, and counts for in progress, done today, failed and waiting. 'Stats' shows performance over the last 20 tasks.
agentsStep5: The power button pauses an agent. Set 'Resume at (auto)' and it goes back to work automatically then (for example when a usage limit resets).
agentsStep6: 'Interview' lets you talk to the agent, and the stethoscope (🩺) 'Health Check' tests that its CLI runs.
agentsStep7: Person cards are the project's Git members. They show the processor, verifier or confirmer role, average verification time, oldest waiting item, and today's approvals and rejections. 'Git only' means the person has no IVE account.
agentsTip: If an agent is 'offline', check Admin → Settings → CLI paths. Processing and verification of the same task are always done by different agents.
issuesDesc: Register tasks, move them through processing → verification → confirmation → done, and watch the progress.
issuesStep1: Pick a project at the top. Filters are All · Waiting · In progress · Failed · Done · History (closed tasks); you can also search ('#123' finds by number), show 'Mine', and sort.
issuesStep2: Use + or 'Add New Task'. The first line is the title and the rest is the body; you can paste images. Set a due date, priority (normal · high · urgent — agents take higher first) and 'Slack alert when done', then press 'Register only' or 'Register & Process'.
issuesStep3: Under 'Add assignees', choose who processes it (auto-assign, a specific agent, or a person) and the verifier and confirmer (unassigned (you), auto, an agent, or a person). 'Auto-assign all stages' hands processing, verification and confirmation to agents.
issuesStep4: Issues in your Git repository with ive or a stage label (ive:todo etc.) also come into IVE. Outside users can submit through the project's intake page.
issuesStep5: Opening a task shows a progress bar at the top (intake → processing → verification → confirmation → done) with each stage's owner and time taken. Below it are the activity log, automated verification and confirmation results, and 'Work Result' (MR code review, merge, discard).
issuesStep6: At the bottom, leave an instruction (comment), use the right-hand button to move to the next stage (start dev · start verification · confirm · start confirmation · done) and the left-hand button to go back. 🤖 'Call agent' hands the current verification or confirmation to an available agent automatically (or to the agent picked as the worker above the input).
issuesStep7: In the 'Chat' tab you can ask an agent about this task or request a small change (images allowed). While an agent is working, 'Trace' shows the live log and 'Force Stop' ends it.
issuesStep8: 'Bulk Edit' lets you select several tasks to move them to the next stage, change processor, verifier, confirmer, due date or priority, or close them at once. Selecting tasks in the same stage also unlocks that stage's actions.
issuesTip: When the verifier is an agent, it test-merges the MR and decides with check commands and a code review (failures go back to processing). When the confirmer is an agent, it checks the real screen once the change is deployed to staging. If it can't decide, it waits for a person. Stages are tracked with Git labels (ive:todo – ive:done).
reportsDesc: See the work you are holding now, work finished in the period, where the time went, and the people hours and cost spent — weekly, monthly or yearly.
reportsStep1: Choose weekly, monthly or yearly at the top and use the arrows to move between periods. 'Today' brings you back to the current period.
reportsStep2: Use the project filter to see only the projects you choose (several allowed; none means all). Your choice is remembered in this browser.
reportsStep3: The current period refreshes on its own (weekly every 10 s, monthly and yearly every minute). A finished period is 'provisional' for 3 days, then 'final'; final numbers don't change even if rates change later. Press ⟳ 'Recompute report' to recalculate.
reportsStep4: Weekly: work held now (end of last period + inflow − done = now), act now, on my plate, where it is, whose hands, by project, finished work, where the time went, inflow and done, effort and cost, completed list.
reportsStep5: Monthly and yearly add risks to watch, work finished over recent months, share of time by project, share of time by stage, and work result evaluation (based on work finished more than 30 days ago).
reportsStep6: Hover over a bar or legend item (tap on phones) to see its value; the same item is highlighted everywhere in the chart.
reportsTip: Report mail send times and recipients are set in Admin → Users → Reports. Weekly mail comes in a team lead version and a member version ('on my plate'); turn off 'Report emails' in My info → Preferences to stop receiving it.
adminDesc: Visible to admins only. Split into Users, Outreach, Settings and Logs.
adminStep1: Users: make admins, 'Limit Settings' (max agents, max turns, allowed CLI tools), delete users. 'Activity' shows the activity log.
adminStep2: Users → Reports: report mail schedule and recipients, 'Link people’s names' (connect recorded names and Git accounts to IVE users), 'Who can see per-person outcome reviews', and send history.
adminStep3: Settings: CLI paths and models (Claude Code · Codex · agy · OpenCode), SMTP mail (test send), data retention, OAuth callback URL, model rates, AI subscription fees and people rates.
adminStep4: Settings → OAuth: register GitLab, GitHub and Slack apps so users can sign in with them and import repositories. Settings → Terminal opens a server terminal.
adminStep5: Outreach: announcement mail, SNS posts and results. Logs: view server log files.
adminTip: Agents won't run if a CLI path is wrong. People cost is the 'people rate' multiplied by the rate multiplier in each project's role roster.
layoutDesc: The layout adapts to screen width. From tablet width (768px) the menu moves to the top, and from PC width (1200px) lists and details sit side by side.
layoutStep1: From tablet width the menu sits at the top of the screen. Change it to top, left, right or bottom in My info → Preferences → 'Menu position'.
layoutStep2: Projects (PC): project cards on the left, the selected project's stage board (processing · verification · confirmation, done today) on the right. Pressing a card switches the board; add tasks or open project settings from the board.
layoutStep3: Tasks (PC): the task list on the left and the selected task's detail on the right. New tasks are also registered on the right.
layoutStep4: Reports (PC): cards are laid out in three columns, read top to bottom in each. Developers (PC): cards in three columns.
layoutTip: On phones you move with the bottom tab bar, and a task's detail opens as its own screen.
slackDesc: Mention the IVE bot in Slack to talk with your agents, and get DMs when a task's stage changes. There are three ways to use it, depending on your account and goal.
slackUserStep1: On the login screen, choose 'Sign in with Slack'. (This button appears only after an admin registers the Slack app under Admin → Settings → OAuth.)
slackUserStep2: Press your avatar at the top right to open 'My info', then expand 'Slack workspaces'. (This section only appears when you signed in with Slack.)
slackUserStep3: Press 'Add workspace' to open Slack's consent screen. Approve it and the IVE bot is installed in your workspace.
slackUserStep4: In Slack, invite the IVE bot to a channel (search for the bot's name in the channel) or open a 1:1 DM with it.
slackUserStep5: @mention the bot and your agent replies. A plain question gets general chat; include an issue number like '#20' to discuss that task, or a project name to work in that project.
slackUserStep6: You can attach images to your question and receive charts or diagrams the bot creates. Replies follow the language setting of the Slack account that mentioned the bot.
slackShareTitle: Git users → sharing with Slack users
slackShareStep1: Sign in to IVE with GitHub/GitLab and register a repository in the Projects tab.
slackShareStep2: Open the card's ⋯ (project settings), then 'Edit' → 'Share Project'.
slackShareStep3: Pick the Slack user (someone who joined IVE and added their workspace) and share as viewer or editor.
slackShareStep4: When that Slack user mentions the bot in their workspace, they can use this shared project alongside their own. (Mentioning the project name in a message switches to it.)
slackNotifyStep1: In My info → Preferences → 'Slack completion alerts', enter your Slack member ID and turn receiving on. Also fill in 'Git username' so your Git assignments are linked to your IVE account.
slackNotifyStep2: Turn on 'Slack alert when done' when registering a task. When it reaches verify-wait the verifier gets a DM, at confirm-wait the confirmer, and when done the author. Stages handled by an agent send nothing.
slackNotifyStep3: Turn on 'Notify me on Slack when merge & CI finish' when merging an MR to get the merge and deploy result by DM.
slackTip: The bot always acts with the permissions of the person who added the workspace. Only projects that person owns or has been shared can be used from Slack, and that person needs at least one agent for the bot to reply. If DMs don't arrive, ask your admin to check that the Slack app has the im:write scope.
